research_dossier.title: Sarah's laughter, Isaac's birth promise and Abraham's intercession (Q 11:71–75)
research_dossier.chronology: Genesis preserves an earlier Jewish scriptural narrative, received in Christian traditions; composition history and surviving manuscript dates must be distinguished. Exact source-stratum dates not asserted.
research_dossier.comparative_discussion: Genesis 18:9–15 and Q 11:71–73 share Sarah's laughter and the extraordinary promise of Isaac despite advanced age. Genesis places laughter after Sarah hears the promise; the Quranic sequence has laughter then glad tidings of Isaac and Jacob. Genesis 18:22–33 and Q 11:74 share Abraham's intervention before judgment of Sodom/Lot's people, but Genesis provides a numerical negotiation absent in the Quran. Q 11:75 characterizes Abraham, not a separate named episode.

research_dossier.variant_witnesses: Masoretic Hebrew, Greek Septuagint, Samaritan Pentateuch, Syriac Peshitta and pre-Islamic reception not collated.
research_dossier.dating_caveat: Textual composition, redaction, earliest attestation, and extant codices are distinct dates.
research_dossier.scholarly_interpretations: A common Abrahamic narrative tradition is a defensible comparison; literary direction or an intermediary remains unproven.
